literal: Again he ordered Ang, saying, "If the others do not comply and accept, you may report according to the matter."
idiomatic: He again ordered Ang, saying, "If the others will not obey and accept, report to me as the facts warrant."

literal: " Ang received the order and laughed, saying, "This exactly matches my lifelong wish."
idiomatic: " Ang took the order and laughed. "That is just what I have wished all my life."

literal: " Ang had always been diligent and careful; after receiving the order he was all the more self-warned and exhorted himself, arranging the articles of law, collating ancient and modern — additions and deletions amounted to seven or eight tenths.
idiomatic: " Ang had always been diligent and careful. After the order he redoubled his watch on himself, set out the legal articles, and collated past and present usage — his additions and cuts came to seven or eight parts in ten.

literal: He was transferred to Director of Convicts.
idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of justice.

literal: Ang's nature was pure and stern; whenever he saw those who took bribes he hated them as enemies — hence his handling of cases ran deep in the law, and worldly opinion did not grant him even-handed lenience.
idiomatic: Ang was by nature austere and strict. Anyone he saw taking bribes he hated like an enemy; for that reason his judgments ran deep and hard, and public opinion did not credit him with fairness.

literal: Xianzu visited Eastern Mountain; all officials attended the feast and ascended the shooting hall.
idiomatic: Gao Yang visited Eastern Mountain. The hundred officials joined the feast and went up to the shooting hall.

literal: The emperor summoned Ang before the imperial seat and said, "Old men mostly go out as provincial governors; I wish to entrust matters within the terrace offices — I shall use you as director and vice director of the secretariat. Do not hope for an inspector's post."
idiomatic: The emperor called Ang before the throne and said, "The old hands mostly go out to the provinces. I mean to put the terrace offices in your hands — you shall serve as director and vice director of the secretariat. Do not look for a provincial inspectorship."

literal: After you turn sixty I shall give you your native province; in between you cannot have a province."
idiomatic: After you pass sixty I will give you your home province. Between now and then you will not get one."

literal: Later, when the nine ministers and above gathered with the crown prince at the Eastern Palace, the emperor pointed to Ang, Wei Jin, and Sima Zirui and said to the crown prince, "These are the pillars of the state — you should remember them."
idiomatic: Later, when the nine ministers and above attended the crown prince at the Eastern Palace, the emperor pointed to Ang, Wei Jin, and Sima Zirui and told the heir, "These are the state's pillars. Mark them well."

literal: Before long he again attended a feast at Golden Phoenix Terrace; the emperor went through the men one by one — all had crimes and faults — until Ang, and said, "Cui Ang is a straight minister, Wei Shou a talented scholar — wife's brother and sister's husband — both are spared blame."
idiomatic: Before long he again attended a feast at Golden Phoenix Terrace. The emperor went down the roster, charging each man with some fault, until he came to Ang and said, "Cui Ang is a straight minister; Wei Shou is a man of letters — brothers-in-law, both of you are excused."

literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao, at the ceremony appointing Yan Zixian as equal in insignia with opening office, the hundred offices formed the escort — Ang was in the ranks.
idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianbao, at the ceremony investing Yan Zixian as equal in insignia with opening office, the hundred offices lined the route — Ang stood among them.

literal: The emperor specially summoned Ang to the imperial place and said, "Having reviewed all the ministers who could keep order in the secretariat, I rely on you alone."
idiomatic: The emperor called Ang alone to the throne room and said, "I have weighed every minister who could keep order in the secretariat. I rely on you alone."

literal: That same day he was appointed acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: That same day he was made acting right vice director of the secretariat.

literal: A few days later Ang came in to report affairs; the emperor said to Director of the Secretariat Yang Yin, "Yesterday I did not give Cui Ang the full appointment — I said it was too fast and intended to make it formal next year."
idiomatic: A few days later Ang came in on business. The emperor said to Yang Yin, director of the secretariat, "Yesterday I did not give Cui Ang the full post — I said it was too soon and meant to make it formal next year."

literal: "In the end formal appointment is formal appointment — what does early or late matter? He may be given the full vice director post."
idiomatic: "A full appointment is a full appointment — what does early or late matter? Give him the full vice directorship."

literal: The next day Ang was immediately invested in the full post.
idiomatic: The next day he was invested at once in the full rank.

literal: Yang Yin had been on bad terms with Ang since youth; after Xianzu's death he removed Ang from vice director and made him equal in insignia to three departments.
idiomatic: Yang Yin had been at odds with Ang since they were young. After Gao Yang's death he stripped Ang of the vice directorship and made him equal in insignia to three departments.

literal: Later he was struck from the rolls for an offense.
idiomatic: Later he was struck from the rolls for an offense.

literal: He died as Director of the Office for Sacrifices.
idiomatic: He died as director of the office for sacrifices.

literal: Ang had elegant bearing and talent with discernment; he had long established a name for firm uprightness and directness.
idiomatic: Ang had presence, talent, and judgment; he had long borne a name for firm, upright conduct.

literal: Yet he liked to probe and gauge the ruler's intent, moved by gratitude to the times' lord; he would sometimes list private crimes and faults, deeply known and rewarded by Xianzu, who spoke to praise and shield him — none could bring him down.
idiomatic: Yet he liked to read the ruler's mind and repay the favor of his times; he would sometimes set out men's hidden faults, and Gao Yang knew and prized this, speaking up to praise and shield him so that none could bring him down.

literal: Council deliberations on laws and statutes, secret prisons of the capital region, and great affairs of court were largely entrusted to him.
idiomatic: Deliberations on law, the capital's secret prisons, and the weightiest court business were largely left to him.

literal: He prized severity and harshness, liked to apply the lash; though suffering was manifold, he faced it with composure.
idiomatic: He favored severity and the whip; though pain ran to every extremity, his face stayed calm.

literal: At first Cui Xian and Ji Shu were his close backers; later Gao Dezheng was his cousin — he always had backing and his manner was proud and lofty, and for this the leading circles did not esteem him.
idiomatic: At first Cui Xian and Cui Jishu backed him closely; later his cousin Gao Dezheng was his patron. He always had someone behind him and carried himself high — for that the leading men did not respect him.

literal: His son Ye succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Ye succeeded him.

literal: The complete text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
